scholarships.title: Barbara Wood Memorial Foundation Scholarship
scholarships.official_source: Barbara Wood Memorial Foundation, administered by the New Zealand Federation of Women's Institutes

existing.description: The Barbara Wood Memorial Foundation provides financial assistance to tertiary students born in the South Pacific region who want to study in New Zealand or elsewhere in the South Pacific. Scholarships of up to NZD 1,000 a year are granted according to the need and cost of the course, at the discretion of the Foundation's trustees. Successful recipients may apply again in any subsequent year. The Foundation was established in memory of Barbara Wood MBE, a former Dominion President of the New Zealand Federation of Country Women's Institutes who died in the Mt Erebus air disaster, and the programme is administered by the New Zealand Federation of Women's Institutes.
eligibility: Be a tertiary student, female or male
Have been born in the South Pacific region, meaning the Pacific island nations as well as New Zealand and Australia
Wish to study in New Zealand or anywhere in the South Pacific region
existing.eligibility_summary: Open to tertiary students of any gender who were born in the South Pacific region, which the Federation defines as the Pacific island nations as well as New Zealand and Australia, and who wish to study in New Zealand or anywhere in the South Pacific.
benefits: Up to NZD 1,000 per year toward course costs
Can be held in consecutive years, because recipients successful in one year may apply again
Open to study anywhere in New Zealand or the wider South Pacific region
coverage: Financial assistance of up to NZD 1,000 a year toward the cost of the course
Award sized according to the need and cost of the course being undertaken
requirements: Submit the completed official application form for the relevant academic year
Send in all papers required by the Conditions for Application, which the Federation states must be followed
Applications are not accepted without a completed official application form plus the information in the Conditions for Application
documents: Completed official Barbara Wood Memorial Foundation application form for the 2027 academic year
All papers listed in the Conditions for Application, which the Federation publishes as a separate document and states must be read and followed
Evidence of being born in the South Pacific region
Evidence of need and of the cost of the course being undertaken
application_method: Download the Conditions for Application document and read it, as the Federation states it outlines what must be sent with the application
Download the application form for the 2027 academic year
Complete the form, attach every required paper, and send the application so it arrives before 1 February 2027
existing.selection_notes: Scholarships are granted at the discretion of the trustees of the Barbara Wood Memorial Foundation, and the amount awarded depends on the need and the cost of the course being undertaken. Applications that are not supported by a completed official application form and the full set of papers in the Conditions for Application are not accepted.
existing.best_fit: A tertiary student born in the Pacific islands, New Zealand or Australia who is studying, or intends to study, in New Zealand or elsewhere in the South Pacific and has demonstrable financial need relative to the cost of their course.
existing.notes: The five successful applicants for the 2026 round were enrolled in a Bachelor of Applied Social Work, a Diploma of Mental Health and Addictions, a Diploma of Veterinarian Nursing, a Bachelor of Midwifery and a Bachelor of Science, which shows the award covers vocational diploma and bachelor's level study in practice. The Federation states that applications will not be accepted without the completed official form plus everything in the Conditions for Application.
existing.duration: Annual award; recipients successful in one year may apply again in any subsequent year
existing.application_period: Applications for the 2027 academic year are open, with an application form published for that year. Applications close on 1 February 2027. Applications for the 2026 academic year have closed.
existing.program_type: Charitable trust scholarship (South Pacific-born tertiary students)

scholarships.title: New Horizons for Women: Hine Kahukura Education Awards
scholarships.official_source: New Horizons for Women: Hine Kahukura

existing.description: The Education Awards are an annual programme of sponsored grants from the New Zealand charitable trust New Horizons for Women: Hine Kahukura, supporting women returning to or continuing education. Awards are sized by qualification level, at NZD 1,000 for NZQCF levels 3-4, NZD 1,500 for levels 5-6 and NZD 3,000 for level 7. Targeted streams exist for refugee and migrant women, STEM degree students, trade and apprenticeship women, solo parents, and Pasifika women in Early Childhood or Primary Education.
eligibility: Be enrolled in an NZQA or Universities New Zealand approved tertiary qualification for study in 2027, in any field of study
Be a New Zealand citizen, or be ordinarily resident in New Zealand and either have lived here on a resident-class visa for at least three years, or be a refugee or protected person of New Zealand
Be studying at certificate level (NZQCF level 3-4), diploma level (NZQCF level 5-6) or degree level (NZQCF level 7)
Have not previously received a New Horizons for Women: Hine Kahukura award at the level of study being applied for
Not be enrolled in secondary school at the time of applying, unless enrolled as an adult student
existing.eligibility_summary: Women enrolled in an NZQA or Universities New Zealand approved tertiary qualification for study in 2027 in any field, at certificate, diploma or degree level, who are New Zealand citizens or ordinarily resident in New Zealand and either have lived here on a resident-class visa for at least three years or are a refugee or protected person of New Zealand, and who have not previously received a Trust award at that level.
benefits: A one-off grant of NZD 1,000 to NZD 3,000 depending on qualification level
Access to targeted award streams for refugee and migrant women, Pasifika women, STEM women, trade and apprenticeship women, and solo parents
Support for non-traditional study fields and for women who have shown community leadership
coverage: NZD 1,000 for study at NZQCF levels 3-4 (certificate)
NZD 1,500 for study at NZQCF levels 5-6 (diploma)
NZD 3,000 for study at NZQCF level 7 (degree)
requirements: Successful applicants must provide certified evidence of their 2027 course enrolment and identity before receiving the money
Must not previously have received a Trust award at the same level of study
documents: Certified evidence of 2027 course enrolment, required before payment
Certified identity evidence, required before payment
Application form as specified by the Trust for the round
application_method: Watch the Trust's Education Awards page for the next opening date, since the current round is closed
Apply using the Trust's application process for the round
Supply certified evidence of 2027 enrolment and identity once selected, before funds are released
existing.selection_notes: The Trust states it is not looking for perfect grades and instead values determination and potential to complete the programme. Selection emphasis is on academic potential and commitment to education, background information including reasons for returning to education and future study or employment goals, and the impact the award will have on the applicant's success.
existing.best_fit: A woman entering or continuing certificate, diploma or degree study in New Zealand in 2027, especially a woman returning to education, a refugee or migrant, or a Pasifika woman.
existing.notes: The maximum is NZD 3,000 at degree level and less at certificate and diploma; value may change yearly with funds available. Sponsors include the Alexandra Kilpatrick Fund, Edward Kay Charitable Trust and Graduate Women North Shore Charitable Trust.
existing.duration: One-off award for a single qualification; a previous recipient cannot apply again at the same level of study
existing.application_period: The Trust's Education Awards page states 'Applications are CLOSED' and that all applications will receive a response in October 2026, for study in 2027. No next opening date is published on the Trust's own site.
existing.deadline_display: Applications closed for the current round; outcomes notified October 2026
existing.program_type: Charitable trust grant programme (women returning to education, with targeted streams for refugee, migrant, Pasifika, STEM, trade and solo-parent students)
